newsitem.title: USA: Helsinki may be the summit of the invalids.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki may be the summit of the invalids.

text.p: If U.S. President Bill Clinton is able to make it to Helsinki next week for his scheduled meeting with Russian President Boris Yeltsin, it may well be the summit of the invalids.
It was Yeltsin's slow recovery from heart surgery and pneumonia that led the United States to agree to a summit in Finland instead of Washington.
Now Clinton has a leg injury that will leave him on crutches for some time to come. He will have surgery on Friday to repair a torn tendon in his right leg after a late-night fall.
So if the two leaders do meet and are unable to agree on issues such as expansion of the NATO alliance, at least they will be able to talk about their recovery efforts.
White House officials were working on the assumption that Clinton still wanted to go on the March 19-20 summit but said a final decision would depend on how he felt after surgery.
"He's indicated that he clearly wants to go and we're proceeding on that assumption and we'll be following things very carefully," said White House spokesman David Johnson.
